graph_convolutional_network.summary: Treats every feature column as a node linked to the columns it moves with, and lets each node average in its neighbours' recent history through normalised graph convolutions before one readout makes the call.
graph_convolutional_network.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the sigmoid of the network's own logit. Differs from the spec: nodes are this model's feature columns and edges are train-span correlations; there is no multi-asset graph. A node holds its last sequence_length values plus a learned identity; layers are ReLU(D^-1/2 (A+I) D^-1/2 H W). Expect: the graph only regroups this bar's own features; no edge over a plain network is assured.

native.produces: For every node of a market graph (a currency pair or a time step), a class probability for its next move read from features averaged over its neighbours through the degree-normalised adjacency with self-loops, or one pooled prediction for the whole graph; the regression variant emits a price estimate instead.
native.targetVariable: The direction of each node's next price move, or in the regression variant its size, where a node is a currency pair or a time step joined to others by thresholded correlation or temporal edges.
native.objectiveNote: The specification leaves the loss task-specific and writes mean squared error for a price target before cross-entropy for classes; the graph convolution adds no loss term of its own, because its neighbour averaging uses fixed degree-normalised weights and only the layer weight matrices are learned.

metrics.why: The class head reads node features that each convolution layer has averaged over the normalised adjacency and is fitted by plain cross-entropy, so the same score on unseen graphs is the direct test of what the neighbour averaging bought.
metrics.baseline: Quoting the training up share of the same series on every scored node.

metrics.why: The convolution claims that a node is better predicted once its neighbours' features are mixed in, so the reference is the same layers with the adjacency replaced by the identity, which leaves each node reading only itself.
metrics.baseline: The same network with the adjacency matrix replaced by the identity matrix, on the same folds.

metrics.why: Averaged node features usually give cautious odds, and the squared miss grades those small departures from the base rate on a bounded scale that one confident wrong node cannot dominate.
metrics.baseline: The squared miss of quoting the training up share of the same series on every scored node.

metrics.why: Each convolution pulls a node's logit toward its neighbourhood's common level, so whether up nodes still sort above down nodes is asked separately from whether the scale of the stated odds is right.
metrics.baseline: One half, the value of an ordering that carries no information.

metrics.why: The specification names accuracy among its classification metrics, so the hit rate of calling a node up when the probability read from the convolved node features is at least one half is read natively too, as the mean of the recall on up nodes and on down nodes so that the base rate of the series does not flatter it.
metrics.baseline: One half, the value of a call that carries no information about the direction.

metrics.why: Stacked neighbour averaging shrinks the spread of the logits while a long fit stretches it again, and the slope shows without bins which of the two pulls won.
metrics.baseline: One, the slope of a probability whose scale is right.

metrics.why: The regression variant the Training section writes first fits each node's next price by mean squared error, and its fair score is how much of the squared miss of forecasting no change the convolved features remove.
metrics.baseline: Forecasting no move on the same resolved nodes.

metrics.why: Too many convolution layers on a dense graph over-smooth until every node carries the same features, and a spread of probabilities near zero is how that collapse shows up.

The adjacency is built by thresholding correlations between pairs and is never learned, so the share of edges that return when it is rebuilt on the next window says whether the fixed wiring the convolution averages along is a stable fact.
Natively the cross-entropy is one quantity on training and held-out graphs, so a widening gap shows the layer weight matrices memorising the training window despite the smoothing.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the gap of a fit that does as well on unseen graphs as on its own.

notApplicable.name: Gaussian NLL Loss
notApplicable.why: The specification's objective is mean squared error or cross-entropy and its head outputs no variance, so a Gaussian likelihood was never this model's loss.

notApplicable.name: Top-Decile Directional Edge
notApplicable.why: Hit rate on only the most confident slice is a selected subset with no registry definition, and the ranking it tries to show is already measured over every node by the receiver operating characteristic area.

notApplicable.name: Gaussian negative log-likelihood
notApplicable.why: The head emits a class probability or one price estimate per node and no variance, so there is no forecast density whose likelihood could be scored.

notApplicable.name: Attention weight entropy
notApplicable.why: The graph convolution weighs neighbours by fixed degree-normalised adjacency entries and learns no attention coefficients, so there is no attention distribution to describe.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: The network states a probability, not a position, so any return per unit of risk belongs to the trading rule and costs applied to its call and is an as-run number only.

asRun.standInNote: The specification builds its graph over currency pairs, but a Model Cycle run holds one instrument, so the nodes of the feature graph are this instrument's feature columns and its edges are the strongest absolute correlations between columns, refitted on each fold's training span; each column's recent values plus a learned identity form its node state, the layers follow the specification's degree-normalised averaging with self-loops, and one graph-level readout gives a single prediction per bar, so the as-run numbers measure a fixed regrouping of this bar's own features rather than cross-market information.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the sigmoid of the single logit the head reads from the pooled node states after the graph convolutions (mean over columns, maximum over columns and a learned weighted sum joined together), with no calibration map, after a fit whose loss weights up bars by the ratio of down bars to up bars in the training span.

meaningful.why: The convolution network was fitted with up and down bars each carrying half the loss, so the score that gives each class half the weight on test bars is the one that matches what its sigmoid output was trained to state.

The logit read from column states averaged over the correlation graph is continuous, and how well it orders up bars above down bars does not depend on the even prior the class weighting centred it on.

This is what the sign of the convolution network's logit earned after costs under the engine's rule of following the latest call and filling at the next open; only the side of one half the probability falls on reaches it.
Subtracting what simply holding the same instrument earned over the same folds shows whether the calls made from the graph-averaged features added anything beyond the drift of the series.

The per-bar profit of following the convolution network's call, costs included, divided by its variability, describes how steadily the direction calls paid; zero is an arithmetic marker here, not a no-skill reference, because a random caller still pays costs.
The deepest fall of the equity built from the convolution network's calls shows the worst stretch a trader following the sign of its logit would have sat through.
Winning trades' dollars over losing trades' dollars for trades that end when the convolution network's call flips, so it reflects how often the logit changes sign as much as how right it is.
The share of closed trades that made money after costs; a trade lasts until the convolution network's call flips, so this counts flips that paid, not bars predicted correctly.
Because a repeated call keeps the position open, the count shows how often the sign of the convolution network's logit flipped, which is needed to read every trading number above.
The share of bars the convolution network called up shows whether its profit is a real two-sided call or a one-sided lean that happened to match the trend of the fold.

The hit rate of calling up when the sigmoid of the convolution network's logit is at least one half; for this class-weighted fit one half means above an even prior, not above the series' own up share.
It sets the convolution network's hit rate against always calling the fold's training majority class on the same bars, the same-series reference that a bare accuracy lacks.
Averaging the recall on up bars and on down bars matches a fit in which each class carried half the loss, so it is the hard-call number most in line with how the convolution network was trained.
One symmetric number over all four cells of the call table, which stays near zero when the convolution network calls a single side on every bar even if that side happened to be common.

The bounded squared miss of the convolution network's sigmoid output on test bars; it is read knowing the class weighting shifted the output toward an even prior, which costs a little when the series leans one way.

The unweighted score of the sigmoid output on test bars is the same quantity that chose the kept epoch on validation bars, and it carries a built-in penalty because the weighted fit centred the output on an even prior rather than the series' up share.
Repeated averaging over the correlation graph narrows the spread of the logits, and the slope asks whether that spread is right without bins and without being moved by the shift toward an even prior.
Stacked graph convolutions can smooth the column states until the pooled readout barely leaves one half, and the spread of the probability shows whether that over-smoothing happened.

This grades a second convolution network of the same design, fitted separately with Huber loss on the volatility-scaled move, against forecasting no change on the same bars; it does not test the direction network.
The typical miss in points of the separately fitted price network of the same graph convolution design, after its output is multiplied back by the trailing move scale and rounded to the tick.

The share of bars where the sign of the second convolution network's forecast matched the move; it can disagree with the traded call because the two networks are fitted separately on different targets.
The size of the gradient before clipping through the convolution weight matrices each epoch shows whether training was stable or was being held together by the clip.
The curvature of the weighted loss around the kept weights describes whether the convolution network settled in a wide valley or a narrow one that the next fold may miss.
The score that picked the neighbour count, hidden size and layer count on inner blocks of the training span; it is a selection score and flattering by construction, shown only beside the test result.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The weighted fit centres the sigmoid output on an even prior, so its gap from the observed up share in each bin is partly built in and does not show a fault of the convolution network.
The largest bin gap inherits the same built-in shift toward an even prior and usually comes from a thinly filled bin, so it says nothing about the convolution network itself.
The intercept measures an overall lean toward up or down, and weighting the classes equally moves it by construction whenever the training span was not evenly split.
The training curve holds the class-weighted loss and the validation curve holds the unweighted logarithmic loss, so their gap compares two different quantities and is not an overfit measure.
With long-only off and no stop or target the engine is always long or short once the first call is made, so the share of bars in the market describes the engine's rule and not the network.

caveats: The feature graph's nodes are this instrument's feature columns and its edges are refitted on each fold's training span, so no cross-market information enters the model.

Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label looks several bars ahead, so any interval on these numbers needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a simple binomial interval.
The kept epoch is the one with the lowest unweighted logarithmic loss on the validation bars, so validation loss is optimistic and only the test walk is out of sample.
The price forecast comes from a second network of the same design fitted with Huber loss and kept on validation Huber loss, not from the direction network.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.
For any root other than MNQ the costs charged are the MNQ account figures applied as a stated assumption.

spatiotemporal_fusion_network.summary: A spatial branch reads the feature graph at every bar, a temporal LSTM reads that sequence of snapshots, and a learned gate decides at the last bar how much each branch drives the call.
spatiotemporal_fusion_network.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the sigmoid of the network's own logit. native.produces: One forecast number per bar, read by a dense layer from a state that fuses a graph network's snapshot of how related assets stand at that bar with a recurrent network's memory of how those snapshots evolved.
native.targetVariable: The future value of the series at the forecast step, such as the coming price or return of an asset in the graph.
native.objectiveNote: The specification minimises the mean squared miss of the dense layer's forecast from the fused spatial and temporal state, optionally after pretraining each branch and with helper losses such as reconstruction.

metrics.why: The graph branch, the recurrent branch and the fusion layer are all trained together to shrink the squared miss, so the fair out-of-sample reading is how much of the squared size of the realised move the fused forecast removes compared with forecasting no move.
metrics.baseline: The no-change forecast on the same resolved bars of the same series.

metrics.why: It restates the network's own training loss in points, so a trader sees how far the dense layer's forecast from the fused state typically lands from the realised move on unseen bars.
metrics.baseline: The root mean square size of the realised move on the same bars, which is the error of forecasting no move.

metrics.why: It checks whether bars where the fused state calls for a bigger move are followed by bigger moves, which can hold even when the scale of the dense layer's output is off.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the value when the forecast carries no linear relation to the realised move.

metrics.why: A recurrent branch trained through a trending stretch can learn to lean one way on every bar, and this mean signed miss shows whether the fused forecast carries such a lean into the test bars.
metrics.baseline: Zero points, a forecast with no lean in either direction.

metrics.why: The spatial branch passes messages along the edges of a graph, so when those edges are estimated from data this shows how many of them reappear when the graph is rebuilt on the next stretch of history, since a link that vanishes cannot be a lasting relation between assets.

The squared error by step on training and validation rows shows whether the stacked graph and recurrent branches kept learning together or whether one branch stalled, and it is read as training health and never as a score of the forecast.

It is the total gradient size over all weights of the network, and the specification calls for gradient clipping to keep the recurrent layers stable, so a sudden rise by step shows instability in the recurrent or graph layers without saying which of the two caused it.

notApplicable.name: Directional Edge
notApplicable.why: The specification trains the dense layer on the size of the miss, not on a hit or miss of direction, so a direction hit rate with a pass mark is not this network's own measure and is reported only as run.

notApplicable.name: Confidence Edge
notApplicable.why: The specified network states a forecast number and no conviction about direction, so there are no conviction deciles for a ranking score to separate.

notApplicable.name: Gaussian NLL Loss
notApplicable.why: The specification's objective and pseudocode use the mean squared error of a single forecast, and a distribution output is mentioned only as an option that is never trained, so the Gaussian likelihood was stamped on by the generator.

notApplicable.name: Top-Decile Directional Edge
notApplicable.why: Cutting out the most confident tenth of bars needs a stated confidence, and the specified network outputs only a forecast number, so this slice and its pass mark were invented by the generator.

notApplicable.name: Brier Score
notApplicable.why: A Brier score grades a stated probability, and natively this network states a forecast size with no probability attached, so it applies only to the runnable adapter's sigmoid output.

notApplicable.name: Brier score
notApplicable.why: The specified network outputs a forecast number under squared error and states no probability of up, so a probability score applies only to the runnable adapter, which ends in a sigmoid.

notApplicable.name: Expert usage shares
notApplicable.why: The fusion step blends one spatial readout with one temporal state and does not route bars among competing experts, so there are no expert shares to report.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: The specification describes a forecaster with no trading rule, position size or cost, so a return per unit of risk appears only once the Model Cycle trades the sign of the call.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable network keeps the specification's three parts, graph convolutions at every bar, a long short-term memory network over those snapshots and a learned logistic gate that fuses the two at the last bar, but the feature graph's nodes are this instrument's feature columns and its edges are refitted on each fold's training span from the correlations between those columns, so there is no graph of related assets, and the head is a sigmoid trained on class-weighted cross-entropy for direction instead of a forecast under squared error, so the as-run numbers measure a regrouping of one bar's own features.
asRun.probabilityNote: The fusion gate mixes the spatial readout of the last bar's feature graph with the recurrent state at that bar, a linear head turns the mix into one logit, and the probability of up is the sigmoid of that logit after training with a positive-class weight equal to the training count of down bars over up bars.

meaningful.why: The fused network is trained with up bars and down bars each carrying half the loss, so its sigmoid output is centred on an even prior, and this score grades the stated odds on that same footing, read against the natural logarithm of two that quoting one half on every bar would give.

The logit from the gated mix of the graph readout and the recurrent state is a continuous score, so this shows whether it orders up bars above down bars regardless of the class weighting that shifted its scale.

The kept epoch is the one with the lowest unweighted value of this quantity on validation rows, so the test value is worth reading, with the warning that the class-weighted training pulls the odds toward an even prior and away from the series' own up share.
It grades the same sigmoid output on a bounded scale, so a handful of bars where the fusion gate left the network almost certain cannot dominate it the way they dominate a logarithmic score.

A deep stack of graph convolutions and a recurrent layer that learned nothing outputs nearly the same logit on every bar, and this spread shows at once whether the fused network ever commits away from one half.

The hard call is up when the sigmoid of the fused logit is at least one half, which under class weighting means above the even prior, so the hit rate is read against calling every bar the fold's training majority direction.

The class weighting was put there so the network cannot win by calling the more common direction, and averaging the hit rate on up bars and on down bars tests the calls on the same footing the loss used.
It sums up in one symmetric number whether the sign of the fused logit moves with the actual direction, with zero meaning the graph and recurrent branches together found nothing.
It is the money made by going long when the sigmoid of the fused logit is at least one half and short otherwise under the engine's fill rule and costs, read against buy and hold on the same folds.

It measures how steadily the sign of the fused logit earned money per bar after costs, and it is also what the hyperparameter search steered the neighbour count, layer count and hidden size toward on training blocks.

It shows the deepest hole dug while following the fused call, which matters because the correlation graph is frozen at the training span and the calls keep using it after the relations between the feature columns have moved.
It compares what the winning trades opened by the fused call made with what the losing ones gave back after costs, read with the trade count because a call that rarely flips produces few trades.
It counts how many trades opened when the fused call flipped ended in profit after costs, which describes the shape of the trading result and is not a direction hit rate.
It counts how often the fused logit crossed zero, since a position is kept while the call stays on one side, and every trading number of this network is read with it.
Class weighting should leave the calls split roughly evenly between up and down, so a share far to one side shows the fused network drifted on the test bars.

The forecast line comes from a second network of the same graph, recurrent and gate design trained separately on Huber loss, so this tests that second network's size forecasts against forecasting no move and says nothing about the traded call.
It gives in points the typical miss of the second, separately trained fusion network's forecast, read beside the no-change forecast's miss on the same bars.
It checks the sign of the separately trained regression network's forecast, which shares no weights with the classifier that makes the traded call, so the two can disagree on a bar.

It is the total gradient size over every weight of the network, taken before clipping and averaged over an epoch's batches, so by step it shows whether training was stable or exploding at all, and it cannot say how much of that signal reached the graph convolutions.
It describes how narrow the valley around the kept weights of the fused network is, which hints at how much a small shift in the features between training and test bars could move the logit.

It is the selection score that chose the neighbour count of the graph, the hidden size, the layer count and the learning rate on training blocks, flattered by that choosing and shown only beside the test value.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The class-weighted loss centres the sigmoid output on an even prior by design, so comparing it bin by bin with the series' actual up share reports that built-in offset and not a fault of the fused network.
The overall lean it measures is the gap between the even prior the class weighting imposes and the series' own up share, which is present by construction.
Its reference is the hindsight up share of the scored test bars, while the network's odds are centred on an even prior, so the comparison mixes two different base rates.
The training curve holds the class-weighted cross-entropy and the validation curve holds the unweighted logarithmic loss, so their difference is offset by construction and is not an overfitting gap.
With the long-only setting off and no stop or target the engine holds a position on every bar once the first trade is open, so this share describes the engine's rule and not the network.

caveats: The feature graph's nodes are this instrument's feature columns and its edges are refitted on each fold's training span, so the spatial branch only regroups one bar's own features and no gain over a plain network on the same columns is assured.
The price forecast is produced by a second, separately trained network of the same design, so price forecast numbers and the traded call can point in different directions on the same bar.
Because of the class weighting a probability of one half means above the even prior and not above the series' own up share, so every hard-call number depends on that fitted prior.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label looks several bars ahead, so intervals around these numbers need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.

The trading numbers follow the run's own long-only, holding bars, stop loss ticks, take profit ticks and contracts settings, the last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next open, and for roots other than the micro Nasdaq contract the cost figure is that contract's figure applied as a stated assumption.

latent_attention_decision_graph.summary: A few learned latents absorb the window by cross-attention, talk to each other over an attention graph, and their summary is routed through a soft decision graph whose leaves each hold a vote.
latent_attention_decision_graph.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the sigmoid of the mass-weighted mixture of leaf logits. Differs from the spec: the graph is over learned latents, not instruments; the decision graph is layered (each node routes to every node of the next layer by a softmax gate); routing temperature anneals temperature to final_temperature; soft routing at inference. Expect: leaves specialise only if the entropy penalty keeps them in use.

native.produces: A class probability for the forward-looking label (or a return estimate) formed as the path-mass-weighted mixture of leaf logits, together with the leaf mass vector, the latent adjacency and the dominant routing path.
native.targetVariable: The outcome strictly after the trailing bar window: next-bar direction, a triple-barrier outcome or the forward return, as the specification allows.
native.objectiveNote: The specification trains on cross-entropy against the forward label, or squared error for the return variant, and adds an entropy penalty on the leaf mass distribution so the decision graph cannot collapse onto a single leaf, and it anneals the routing temperature from soft to sharp during training.

metrics.why: The mixture of leaf logits weighted by the mass reaching each leaf is trained by cross-entropy on the forward label, so the same score on unseen bars tests the whole chain from latent cross-attention to routing gates.
metrics.baseline: Quoting the fold's training up share on every scored bar of the same series.

metrics.why: The decision graph is the part that makes this model readable, so it has to be shown that routing the pooled latent through the gates does not score worse than a plain linear head on the same pooled latent.
metrics.baseline: The same latent encoder and message passing with the decision graph replaced by one linear head, on the same folds.

metrics.why: The specification itself names the mass on the busiest leaf as the collapse indicator, and the share of bars each leaf receives says whether the readable paths are really distinct routes or one route with spare leaves.
metrics.baseline: Equal mass on every leaf, the state the zero-initialised gate biases start from.

metrics.why: When the annealed temperature makes routing nearly hard the mixed logit can jump to an extreme leaf value, and the bounded squared miss grades those confident bars without letting a handful dominate.
metrics.baseline: The squared miss of quoting the fold's training up share on every scored bar.

metrics.why: The final routing temperature sets how sharp the mixture of leaves is, so a slope away from one shows directly whether the anneal ended too sharp or stayed too blurred for the stated odds to be believed.
metrics.baseline: One, the slope of a probability whose scale is right.

metrics.why: With few leaves and sharp routing the output takes a limited set of values, so the ordering of bars is checked on its own to see whether the paths separate up bars from down bars at all.
metrics.baseline: One half, the value of an ordering that carries no information.

metrics.why: The specification treats spread-out path mass as a no-trade signal because the mixed output then sits near neutral, so the spread of the probability shows how often the graph commits to a path.
Each latent node reads the bar window through cross-attention, and the entropy of those weights describes whether a latent watches a few bars or smears over the whole window.
metrics.baseline: The natural logarithm of the window length, the entropy of attending to every bar equally.

notApplicable.name: Directional Edge
notApplicable.why: Natively the leaf mixture is judged on the probability it states, and a hit rate needs a cut at one half that the specification never fixes; the hit rate is measured only as run, against the majority-class call of the same series and without the invented pass mark.

notApplicable.name: Gaussian NLL Loss
notApplicable.why: The Algorithm section's objective is cross-entropy or squared error plus a leaf-entropy penalty; no variance is predicted, so a Gaussian likelihood never applied.

notApplicable.name: Volatility-Adjusted RMSE
notApplicable.why: A squared forecast error belongs only to the variant whose leaves hold return estimates; the classification model described first states a probability and forecasts no size.

notApplicable.name: Top-Decile Directional Edge
notApplicable.why: Hit rate on only the most confident slice is a selected subset with no registry definition, and for this model confidence is better read from the mass on the dominant path.

notApplicable.name: Gaussian negative log-likelihood
notApplicable.why: The leaves hold bare logits and the output is one mixed number, so the model states no variance and has no forecast density to score.

notApplicable.name: Training loss against validation loss
notApplicable.why: The training loss includes the leaf-entropy penalty and is taken at that epoch's routing temperature while a validation score has no penalty, so the two are different quantities and their gap is not an overfit measure.

notApplicable.name: Expert usage shares of a gate
notApplicable.why: The leaves here are bare logits reached through several layers of routing, not separate expert networks behind one gate, so leaf mass is reported under the architecture's own routing unit instead.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable network follows the specification's chain of latent cross-attention, message passing over a soft latent adjacency, softmax routing with an annealed temperature and a leaf-entropy penalty, but its decision graph is fixed as layers in which every node sends mass to every node of the next layer, its leaves hold one bare logit for the single up or down question, routing stays soft at inference, the entropy penalty is taken on the batch's mean leaf mass, and the loss weights the classes equally, so the as-run numbers measure that specific layered version answering one binary label.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the sigmoid of the sum over leaves of the path mass reaching each leaf times that leaf's logit, with soft routing at the temperature saved with the kept epoch and no calibration map, after a fit whose loss weights up bars by the ratio of down bars to up bars in the training span.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per bar, with the leaf-entropy penalty added on the training side only

meaningful.why: The leaf mixture was fitted with up and down bars each carrying half the loss, so the score that gives each class half the weight on test bars matches what the mass-weighted leaf logits were trained to state.

Soft routing keeps the mixed leaf logit continuous, and its ordering of up bars above down bars does not depend on the even prior the class weighting centred it on or on how sharp the final temperature left it.

This is what the sign of the mixed leaf logit earned after costs under the engine's rule of following the latest call and filling at the next open; how much mass the winning path carried never reaches it.
Subtracting what simply holding the same instrument earned over the same folds shows whether the decision graph's calls added anything beyond the drift of the series.

The per-bar profit of following the decision graph's call, costs included, divided by its variability, describes how steadily the routed calls paid; zero is an arithmetic marker here, not a no-skill reference, because a random caller still pays costs.
The deepest fall of the equity built from the decision graph's calls shows the worst stretch a trader following the dominant path would have sat through.
Winning trades' dollars over losing trades' dollars for trades that end when the leaf mixture changes sign, so it reflects how often the routing switches side as much as how right it is.
The share of closed trades that made money after costs; a trade lasts until the leaf mixture flips sign, so this counts flips that paid, not bars predicted correctly.
Because a repeated call keeps the position open, the count shows how often the mass moved to leaves of the opposite sign, which is needed to read every trading number above.
If the leaves collapse onto one path the graph calls the same side on nearly every bar, and the share of bars called up exposes that before the profit figure is trusted.
The hit rate of calling up when the sigmoid of the leaf mixture is at least one half; for this class-weighted fit one half means above an even prior, not above the series' own up share.
It sets the decision graph's hit rate against always calling the fold's training majority class on the same bars, the same-series reference that a bare accuracy lacks.
Averaging the recall on up bars and on down bars matches a fit in which each class carried half the loss, and it cannot be inflated by a collapsed graph that sends every bar to one leaf.
One symmetric number over all four cells of the call table, which stays near zero when the routing sends every bar to leaves of a single sign.
The bounded squared miss of the leaf mixture's probability on test bars, which grades the confident outputs a sharp final temperature produces without letting a few of them dominate.

When path mass spreads over many leaves the mixed logit sits near neutral, so the spread of the probability shows how often the graph committed to a route at all.

Path mass is a product of gates, which amplifies instability as the temperature falls, and the size of the gradient before clipping each epoch is where that shows.
